correctness.rationale: The rank-two EF game characterizes each finite word by the SET of all first-picked point characters (letter, set of letters to left, set to right). Duplicator matches the first point exactly iff the two character types have matching letter and left/right sets; every second point is then matchable in either direction. The exact append transition T_a maps each existing (c,L,R) to (c,L,R∪{a}) and appends (a,U,∅), so BFS from empty signature is closed under both a in {0,1} after exactly 97 states; restricting to words containing both letters gives 90 states for arbitrary lengths. Reversal swaps L,R and fixes exactly 20 of the 90; explicit all-palindrome enumeration through length 9 realizes all and only these 20, proving sufficiency. Distribution of shortest palindrome lengths 3:2, 4:2,5:6,6:2,7:6,9:2 follows. Both nine-length extremes have eight distinct characters, including self-reversing center characters for colors 0 and 1; any length-eight palindrome duplicates each such character in mirror pairs and cannot represent all eight, proving sharp nine, while unrestricted length-eight representatives exist. Independent separately-written BFS/characters/direct game verifier reproduced 97/90/20 and the nine-length witnesses; proof rests on state closure, not arbitrary bounded-word extrapolation.
residual_risks: Only two named letters and quantifier rank <=2; no higher-rank/more-color palindrome criterion asserted.
Finite word-length check alone would be invalid, but full 97-state transition closure proves every finite length.

value.rationale: For finite-model theory, asking which logical rank-two theories admit a literal palindrome is a natural symmetry realizability problem, not a renaming of the unrestricted 90-type classification. The exact 20-state fixed-point theorem, complete minimal palindrome-length distribution and sharp extra-length obstruction at nine give a self-contained natural constrained normal-form theorem of plausible downstream use. The nontrivial sufficiency and sharpness are supported by complete transition closure and the EF game lemma.
residual_risks: This is exact low-rank binary-word theory; no claim to higher ranks/general alphabets.

limitations: Rank-two finite two-color nonmonochromatic words only.
